summary:
“THANK YOU, ROVERS” is an interactive, storybook-style website that honors the Mars rovers that still rest on the Red Planet after their missions ended.

It follows three rovers — Sojourner, Spirit, and Opportunity — from their creation and journey to Mars, through their exploration and scientific discoveries, to their final days. Every chapter is built on NASA mission data: real rover images, landing sites, traverse routes, mission timelines, and key findings such as evidence that liquid water once existed on Mars.

With warm watercolor and colored-pencil illustrations and scroll-based animations, visitors travel alongside each rover. Sojourner was planned to work for 7 days but lasted 83. Spirit and Opportunity were planned for 90 days, yet Spirit worked for over 6 years and Opportunity for nearly 15, driving more than 45 km. We turn these facts into emotional stories instead of numbers in a table.

Why it matters: planetary science often feels distant and technical, especially for children and non-specialists. By presenting rovers as characters people can care about, our website makes NASA science approachable, sparks curiosity about space exploration, and shares gratitude for the machines and the people who built them.

The site runs in any web browser with no installation, uses simple language, and is designed for classrooms, museums, and families around the world.
details:
What it does / How it works
“THANK YOU, ROVERS” is an interactive, storybook-style website that tells the life stories of three Mars rovers: Sojourner, Spirit, and Opportunity. Each rover has its own chapter, divided into scenes: Birth (design and building), Journey (launch and landing), Exploration (driving and daily work), Discovery (key scientific findings), and Farewell (the end of the mission). As visitors scroll, illustrations move, text appears, and the rover travels across the page. This makes reading feel like turning the pages of a picture book.

Use of NASA data
The stories are based on NASA mission data: [e.g., rover images from the NASA/JPL Photojournal, mission timelines, landing site and traverse maps, mission facts from NASA Science pages]. Key facts include mission length, distance driven, and discoveries such as evidence of past water on Mars. We checked these against NASA sources so that the emotional story stays scientifically accurate.

Benefits

  • It makes Mars exploration easy to understand for children, students, and people with no science background.
  • It turns numbers (for example, “90 days planned, nearly 15 years achieved”) into memorable stories.
  • It is free, runs in any browser, and needs no installation or account.
  • It can be used in classrooms, museums, and science events.

Intended impact
We want people to feel connected to space exploration, not just learn facts about it. When people care about the rovers as characters, they become curious about the science behind them. We hope the site inspires the next generation of scientists and engineers, and spreads gratitude for the machines and the thousands of people who made these missions possible.

Tools and technologies

  • Language: HTML
  • AI tools: ChatGPT, Gemini, MuseAI, Claude
  • Hosting: GitHub

Creativity
Most rover information is presented as data tables, technical reports, or news articles. We took a different approach: a warm, hand-drawn storybook that treats each rover as a character with a life story. Combining science with picture-book storytelling and scroll-based animation creates an emotional experience that is rarely seen in science communication.

Factors we considered

  • Scientific accuracy: every fact is based on NASA sources.
  • Accessibility: simple language, readable fonts, clear contrast, and a layout that works on phones, tablets, and PCs.
  • Respect: we show the rovers’ mission endings with care, focusing on gratitude rather than sadness.
  • Global audience: the design relies on visuals so it can be enjoyed across ages.
  • Performance: we optimized images and animations so the site runs smoothly in a browser.

Future work

  • Illustrations and artwork: improve the design and quality of the illustrations so each scene feels more like a real picture book.
  • Animation: add richer, smoother scroll-based animations so the rovers’ journeys feel more alive.
  • Multilingual support: translate the site into more languages, starting with Japanese and English, so people around the world can enjoy it.
